text:
Sam: Heads-up: noticed a regression in Mixtral MoE p99 latency after the recent kernel selector change. Router-heavy traces show spike in KV cache churn.

Maya: Can you paste the profiler snippet or a flamegraph link? :eyes:

Sam: Paste from perf -> top hotspots (trimmed):
```
+ 42.1%   mixtral_router::route::compute_logits
+ 18.7%   matmul_kernel_v3::fwd
+ 12.3%   kv_cache::evict
+ 10.5%   softmax::stable
+ 6.9%    expert_dispatch::handshake
```
KV evictions are ~3x the baseline for seq_len=512, batch=8.

Devon: matmul_kernel_v3 was optimized for large head dims (>=64) and fused bw perms. Mixtral uses head_dim=48 in our config, so kernel selection math is picking a less-suitable path -> more copies and higher memory pressure.

Sree: That aligns with the RoPE scaling noise we saw on routing logits. If matmul path increases tail latency, routers timeout and reassign leading to extra kv writes (thrash).

Maya: Quick mitigation ideas: lower router_logit_temp, reduce top_k, and force kernel fallback for head_dim<56. We can also try smoothing logits to avoid oscillation.

Sam: I ran two short experiments locally: smoothing + kernel-fallback (A/B). Results (p95/p99) for seq=512,batch=8:
- baseline: 42ms / 210ms
- kernel-fallback only: 38ms / 160ms
- kernel-fallback + logit_temp=0.8 + top_k=4: 36ms / 120ms
KV evictions dropped ~65% with smoothing.

Devon: Nice. Can you share the toggles you used?

Sam: Config snippet I applied on the canary runtime (yaml):
```yaml
model_overrides:
  mixtral-moe-v1:
    runtime_flags:
      prefer_kernel: "auto" # default was v3
      fallback_kernel_for_head_dim_lt: 56
    router:
      logit_temp: 0.8
      top_k: 4
    serving:
      expert_parallelism: 12  # was 16 on A100-40
      kv_cache_eviction_threshold: 0.75
```

Sree: Reducing expert_parallelism reduces in-flight experts per batch which lowers concurrent KV writes and eviction pressure. Tradeoff is throughput; we should measure steady-state RPS.

Maya: I'll schedule a canary sweep across instance types (a100-40, a100-80, h100) with these permutations:
- kernel fallback on/off
- logit_temp {0.6,0.8,1.0}
- top_k {2,4,8}
- expert_parallelism {8,12,16}
Run workload profile: bursty arrival pattern with seq=128/512, batch sizes 1..16.

infra-bot: Canary canary-20260301 deployed to eng-runtime-canary-2 (a100-40).

Devon: Also add a metric for "expert_handoff_count" (increments whenever router reassigns an active token to a different expert within same request) and "kv_eviction_rate/second" so we can correlate spikes.

Sam: Agreed — I'll open a tiny PR to add the two counters + tag them by model_version and kernel_variant.

Maya: One more note: Watch for softmax numeric differences when we change kernel paths. We saw tiny probability mass shifts that can amplify router decisions under top_k routing. Add an eval run against the stable prompt set.

Sree: For longer-term: update kernel selector cost model to include head_dim and estimated kv-write bytes for MoE dispatch. That should avoid the current mis-choice.

Sam: TL;DR: immediate canary uses kernel fallback + logit smoothing + reduce expert_parallelism. Early numbers look promising (p99 halved). Running full sweep, will post flamegraphs and perf traces here. :rocket:
